fields.reasoning: The finding is confirmed: changeLeavesIn (internal/api/change.go) takes only created capabilities, so the acceptance updates on milestone-request-starts-at-once and request-slot-kept reach no builder or verifier. daemon-starts-within-max-runs is the created leaf whose statement already lists 'a queued milestone request's plan run' among the starts held at the cap, and plan-runs-share-max-runs (3) makes the milestone wait at the cap part of the same one machine-wide count this leaf implements; the code change is one slot count, so splitting the milestone checks into a second created leaf would duplicate a capability and split one implementation across two builders. Both testscripts already exist (daemon-milestone-request.txtar, daemon-request-slot.txtar), so naming them with the exact cases from the updated capabilities' acceptance, and adding daemon-milestone-request to the -run pattern (daemon-request-slot is already in it), is the smallest edit that gives every new check a build that runs it.
fields.statement: Settle it on the existing leaf: @{01M6XVG9DK25PFK9BHJCBDQHQ6}'s acceptance takes over the milestone-at-cap checks written on @{01M6MYSEB8N545M8M9APZTBXYS} and @{01M6HT09X1W6W89R5N272GJXMP}. It names cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/daemon-milestone-request.txtar (with --max-runs 1 and one run live, daemon --once starts nothing and the milestone and feature requests stay queued; with one interrupted run and one free slot the milestone request starts and the run is not resumed) and daemon-request-slot.txtar (with max-runs 2, two ready change sets and only a queued milestone request, daemon --once starts the milestone request's plan run and one ship run, never three, and daemon status shows the other as no-slot), and its go test -run pattern adds daemon-milestone-request. No new created leaf is added for the milestone change.
